rationale: The 279-page proceedings were screened after a font-specific text repair. The sole Melissa-family hit is a contributor's given name in the original p. 51 synaptic-vesicle member, which concerns release and recycling at a cerebellar synapse. No lemon balm name or botanical exposure was identified in the screened text.

The publisher's October volume contains reviewed poster abstracts and ends with Encore title listings. The searchable original has an editor name matching Melissa and no lemon, balm or officinalis text. Omitted member bodies are outside the published supplement and remain unavailable.

The Protein Society volume was checked from its first posted folding abstract through its final chromatin-binding report. Melissa appears in a contributor line and the lemon substring occurs in a place name. No lemon-balm exposure was identified in the published body.

The original ESOC 2024 book spans plaque morphology through its closing outcomes abstract. Melissa-family matches are names, the lemon substring occurs in telemonitoring, and balm matches occur in institutional or contributor names. Those passages contain no lemon-balm comparison.

The published ARO record is a list of podium and poster titles with presenters. The Melissa matches in the checked listing are personal names. The society's companion abstract-book link was unavailable and abstract-level coverage remains open.
